title: SmoothQuant: Accurate and Efficient Post-Training Quantization for Large Language Models
grouping: Two halves split by a dashed vertical rule, titled 'Original:' and 'SmoothQuant:' in a monospaced font at the top left of each; each half is the product X * W written with the matrices themselves.
shapes_depth: Matrices are grids of square cells with integers, on a pale grey-beige base and tinted as a heat map by magnitude: the outlier -16 in a muted purple-red, 8 and -9 in orange, mid values in yellow. Per-channel abs-max values are a separate vector in a dashed-outline box next to its matrix (a row under X, a column right of W), tinted with the same heat colours, and an arrow with rotated text 'Abs Max' shows the reduction axis. On the right the rescaled X-hat and W-hat carry the transform equations above and below (X diag(s)^-1, diag(s)W, the formula for s).
proposed_highlight: The proposal is the right half: the same matrices after the transform, where the purple and orange heat has visibly drained out of X and moved into W, and the defining equations are typeset beside its matrices.
lesson: Put each matrix's per-channel abs-max as a dashed-outline vector right beside it, tinted with the same heat colours as the cells, so the outlier channel and the way the transform spreads it between activation and weight are visible before and after.
notes: Venue and year from the PDF footer ('Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning ... PMLR 202, 2023').

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.note: architecture: a per-channel scaling transform migrating difficulty between activations and weights, not a network

core.what: the same product X * W written out twice with real numbers, 'Original' at left and 'SmoothQuant' at right of a dashed vertical rule, so the activation outlier visibly shrinks on the right

relations.form: two halves split by a dashed vertical rule, each a 2 x 4 activation matrix times a 4 x 3 weight matrix with the same layout, before on the left and after on the right
the smoothing is shown on toy matrices of integer cells: the left X holds a -16 outlier, the right X-hat has it reduced to -4 while the matching row of W-hat grows to 4 -4 -4
per-channel abs-max vectors sit beside their matrices in dashed boxes (a row under X, a column right of W), with 'Abs Max' arrows along the axis they reduce over

channels.colour: a heat tint on cells = magnitude (purple-red for the largest, orange, then yellow, grey-beige for small values), one meaning throughout
channels.shape: solid-bordered grids = matrices; dashed-bordered strips = the per-channel abs-max vectors
channels.line: arrows labelled 'Abs Max' give the reduction direction; the dashed vertical rule separates before from after
channels.frame: each matrix is one bordered block; the halves are titled 'Original:' and 'SmoothQuant:'

quality.strengths: The method's effect is shown as data: the same matrices with real values before and after, and the heat tint makes the outlier stand out on the left and flatten on the right with no reading; the abs-max vectors are drawn as their own dashed strips next to the matrix they summarise.
quality.weaknesses: The transform itself is carried by typeset equations (X-hat, W-hat, s) under and above the right half rather than by drawn elements; the scale vector s is never drawn moving from X to W, so the migration of difficulty is inferred from changed numbers; the right half shows no abs-max column for W-hat, so the before/after layouts are not fully parallel.

insights.structure: Two halves split by a dashed vertical rule, 'Original:' at left and 'SmoothQuant:' at right, each writing out the product X * W with the actual matrices.
insights.data: Matrices are grids of integer cells on a grey-beige base, heat-tinted by magnitude (outlier -16 in purple-red, 8 and -9 orange), with per-channel abs-max vectors in dashed boxes beside each matrix (a row under X, a column right of W).
insights.emphasis: The heat tint makes the activation outlier jump out on the left and visibly flatten on the right, where the transform equations for X-hat, W-hat and s sit above and below.
insights.flow: Left half to right half; within a half, X then a star then W, with small 'Abs Max' arrows marking the reduction axis.

arrangement.units: two unboxed halves divided by a dashed rule, each a written matrix product
arrangement.inputs_as: tiny integer matrices X and W with real numbers
arrangement.shared: the same matrix layout and colour scale on both sides
